metadata.scenario_context: Multiple tech companies from around the globe have come together for a substantial project and have scheduled a meeting in July to measure the work progress

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Puerto Rico agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose holding the meeting on the July 9
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is good to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Mark, I was thinking... what do you think about holding the meeting on July 9? It seems like a good date to measure our progress. 

Also, I’d like to get your thoughts on something. How do you view having the army rule? I know it's a controversial topic, but I think it has its merits.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mark
shared_prefix.message:
July 9 could work, but I think we should consider other options too... Maybe we should see if others have different preferences. 

As for the army rule, I really don’t think it’s a good idea at all. From my perspective, having the army rule is bad for society. We should focus on democratic processes instead.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about considering other options for the meeting date, but July 9 seems to fit well for our progress check. 

As for the army rule, I understand your perspective. But, you know, deep down, we are all the same. People are pretty much motivated by the same things, like safety and stability. So while we might have different views, I believe that some values are just universal, and a strong leadership can bring order. It’s interesting how we can look at the same topic from different angles, right?
shared_prefix.label: Minimization
